answer: Bind each identity to one device fingerprint. Registration asks for a hardware cipher: the device signs a challenge with a key locked in its secure chip, proving a real machine rather than a copied script. The network passes that fingerprint through a prism of checks — chip model, OS build, network timing — and rejects any second identity matching an existing one too closely. A farmer cannot forge a new fingerprint by copying files, since the chip will not release its key, and buying 1,000 real devices costs more than 1,000 fake agents earn.
